name: Pauli's egg dream — spontaneous division, conscious participation and the circle
description: The seven pictures in sequence: the egg laid and self-divided, the egg found in the dreamer's hand, the division that keeps wholeness, four eggs become expressions, the conjugate quotient, and the spoken circle.

text.kicker: #0 · "Modern Examples of 'Background Physics'", Atom and Archetype, pp. 192–196
text.title: A physicist meets his concepts in a dream
text.italic: The dream sequence demonstrates symbolic description arriving in a mode the dreamer did not consciously choose — and his initial finding of it offensive to scientific habit.

text.body: Pauli's egg dream is a sequence of seven pictures. He introduces "background physics" as physical concepts appearing spontaneously in dreams in a qualitative, symbolic sense — initially offensive to his scientific habits, then an inquiry into the psychic activity of such images and the archetypal background of scientific concepts, explicitly distinguished from a formulated body of scientific truths. Two related dreams fall in an interval

of four days in mid-March, after the Kepler work; the later 60P letter dates the first to 1948 and the essay to June 1948. Göttingen belongs to the companion dream, with the changed hydrogen ground state and brass tones on a metal plate. The egg dream names no city, room or landscape; its space is enacted by arrival, approach and the discovery of something already in the dreamer's hand.
Occurrences: the seven-picture sequence (#0–#3); the mid-March pairing and its retrospective dating (#0); the Göttingen companion dream kept distinct (#0); Fierz's undated typescript (#0).

text.kicker: #1 · pp. 192–193; the diagrams as visually checked
text.title: Pictures 1–2: the egg laid; the egg divides itself
text.italic: The dream demonstrates plurality made before agency appears: the division occurs without Pauli's reported intervention.

text.body: Picture 1: a woman comes with a bird; the bird lays a large egg. The account gives neither the woman's name nor the bird's species — nothing in the later formula retroactively supplies them a historical identity. The first diagram shows the single egg, its enclosing outline still the form of one thing awaiting what will happen. Picture 2: the egg

divides itself into two. Pauli's grammatical distinction matters — this division occurs without his reported intervention. Two complete egg outlines stand beside one another; they are not described as a good and an evil egg, and no conflict occurs between them. What changes is the field of the image: one has become two while each remains presented as an egg.
Occurrences: the woman and bird's arrival and laying (#1, no further actions); the self-division (#1); the two-whole-eggs result (#1, mirrored consciously at #2).

scenes.name: Pictures 3–4: the egg in his own hand; division that keeps wholeness
scenes.character: The dreamer goes closer, finds a blue-shelled egg already held, divides it — and the two miraculously remain whole.

entities.name: pictures 1–2 — the spontaneous pair above
picture 3 — the blue-shelled egg in his hand
picture 4 — divided, both whole
the marvel — two eggs, not two broken portions
the dreamer — approaches, notices, participates

text.title: Pictures 3–4: the egg in his own hand; division that keeps wholeness
text.italic: The scene passes from watching a division to performing one upon what he holds — the event on which his later commentary concentrates.

text.body: Picture 3: Pauli goes closer and notices another egg in his hand, this one with a blue shell. The account does not say he manufactures it or takes it from the first pair; the diagram adds the third beneath the two above, changing the count and the dreamer's position. Picture 4: he divides this last egg into two; they miraculously remain whole, and he now has two

blue-shelled eggs. The source records preservation through division as the marvel: two eggs, not two broken portions requiring an invented repair; no hatching, no discarded shell. The two pairs have related but distinct histories — one from spontaneous change witnessed, one from his recognition and action. Its force would disappear if the four eggs were introduced at once as an emblem with four fixed meanings.
Occurrences: the approach and the noticed egg (#2); the performed division and preserved wholeness (#2); the two origins of the four eggs (#1–#2, retained at #4–#5).

scenes.name: Pictures 5–6: four eggs become expressions; the conjugate quotient
scenes.character: The duplicated cos/sin rows form a relation of conjugate expressions — the cosine the same, the imaginary sine term changing sign.

entities.name: picture 5 — four expressions, two rows: cos(δ/2) sin(δ/2) / cos(δ/2) sin(δ/2)
picture 6 — the quotient [cos+i·sin]/[cos−i·sin], modulus one in the denominator
no shell-to-function assignment is added
the opposing signs retained in one relation

text.title: Pictures 5–6: four eggs become expressions; the conjugate quotient
text.italic: The dream's organisation changes from four displayed terms into a single relation that retains their opposing signs — an ordinary, well-defined complex-number operation.

text.body: Picture 5: the four eggs change into four mathematical expressions, printed as two rows each holding a cosine term on the left and a sine term on the right. The duplicated terms preserve the paired arrangement while changing the medium of the scene; the picture does not assign each shell colour to a function, so no such assignment is added.

Picture 6: the terms give the quotient with cos(δ/2)+i·sin(δ/2) over cos(δ/2)−i·sin(δ/2) — the cosine the same while the imaginary sine term changes sign; for real δ the denominator has modulus one. The dream's organisation has changed from four displayed terms into a single relation retaining their opposing signs.
Occurrences: the four-eggs-to-expressions transformation (#3, from the four of #1–#2); the conjugate quotient (#3); the retained opposing signs (#3).

scenes.name: Picture 7: he speaks, and the circle appears
scenes.character: Pauli speaks for the first time: the expression is e^{iδ}; the formula vanishes and a circle appears. Speech enters at the end.

text.kicker: #3 · p. 193; diagrams visually checked in the consulted PDF
text.title: Picture 7: he speaks, and the circle appears
text.italic: The completion demonstrates the history it carries: the final image is circular rather than the initial egg outline, and no unreported eighth scene is needed.

text.body: Picture 7: Pauli speaks for the first time in this dream. He identifies the expression with e^{iδ} and names the circle; the formula vanishes and a circle appears. The explanation makes the step explicit: the quotient equals e^{iδ/2} over e^{−iδ/2}, which is e^{iδ} — for a fixed real angle a point on the unit circle; as the angle varies, the circle.

The distinction keeps the operation exact while preserving what Pauli recognises. The account reports neither a return of the woman and bird nor a restart of the first picture; the completion has the history of differentiation and conscious action within it.
Occurrences: the spoken naming (#3); the vanishing formula and appearing circle (#3); the seven-picture cardinality retained (#0–#3).

text.kicker: #4 · p. 195; pp. 190, 195–196; the harmonised source programme; A19/A16 comparisons
text.title: Pauli reads the part played by consciousness
text.italic: The commentary proves-discloses conscious participation as the change producing the quaternity — while refusing to present a finished interpretation of the two dreams.

text.body: Pauli's commentary joins the two dreams through the intervention absent from the initial pair: the spontaneous pair read as a ground state, his participation in Pictures 3 and 4 producing the quaternity. He relates the sequence to the axiom attributed to Maria Prophetissa via Jung — his comparison, not verified ancient attribution. He gives the imaginary unit a symbolic office permitting paired opposites to combine

into the form he reads as wholeness, and refuses a finished interpretation: further progress in the sciences would be required. Around the essay he distinguishes physical process from psychic symbolic use and marks the limits of physics within life; mathematics has qualitative resources, topology among them, whose symbolic possibilities he considers unfinished. The Neumann whole is compared as shared structuration; a new exact egg-to-stage assignment is human-amplified: no.
Occurrences: the ground-state reading of pictures 1–2 (#1, #4); the intervention reading of 3–4 (#2, #4); the i-office (#3, #4); the refused finished interpretation (#4).

text.kicker: #5→0 · the harmonised quilt line 840/881; A16's complex-phase aperture; human-amplified flags local
text.title: Return: the recovered telling and its authorial office
text.italic: The ending places the dreamer in a different relation to the first appearance — the whole-form QL refraction is developed while its external dependencies are identified.

text.body: The recovered primary telling supplies the seven pictures; the exact separate Taylor egg-specific commentary remains an authorial-carrier debt. Taylor's core theorem field grounds the native relation including all eight determinations — X/x is Taylor's notation, and the egg dream does not supply it: neither seven pictures nor four eggs count as an independently established identity with the eight determinations or the six positions. A19's comparison — the observer

brought into the operation he first receives as a scene before him — is human-amplified: no for the newly specified edge. A16's complex-phase aperture makes the retained-modulus/changed-angle distinction exact without identifying a unit circle with a torus or a theory of psychic causation; the exact egg-to-QL symbolic map remains human-amplified: no. Human-amplified: yes for the already adopted whole-before-fragments programme office; no new symbolic identity is ratified here.
Occurrences: the seven pictures' cardinality (#0–#3, #5→0); the four eggs' two origins (#1–#2, #5→0); the spoken circle (#3, #5→0).
